user.title: Abode Power Tariffs
user.description: One entry per metering channel — general consumption, controlled load, a second circuit. Each is a separate plan with separate prices.

data_description.plan_name: Shown on the device and used as the prefix on every entity.

first_rate.title: Your first rate
first_rate.description:
A rate is a price with a name — peak, off peak, free. You define it once here and point time periods at it later.

Until you add time periods, the whole day is priced at this rate. Nothing is invented: every figure published is one you entered.

data_description.name: As it appears on your bill — for example peak, off peak, shoulder.
data_description.import_cents: Cents per kilowatt hour, as the bill quotes it.
data_description.export_cents: Your feed-in rate. Leave at zero if you do not export.
data_description.daily_supply_charge_cents: The fixed charge per day. Zero if you do not have one.

abort.already_configured: A channel with that name already exists.

rates_menu.title: Rates
rates_menu.description:
A rate is a named price. Define it once; point as many time periods at it as you like, and changing the price changes them all.

```
{rates}
```

rate_add.title: Rate
rate_add.description: Prices are entered in cents per kWh, as bills quote them, and published in dollars per kWh, which is what the Energy dashboard wants.

data.name: Rate name
data.constraints: Rules that apply during this rate
data.coasting_permitted: Good time to stop drawing power
data.demand_period: This is a demand charge period
data.fallback_rate: Rate once the allowance is used up

data_description.constraints: Comma separated, your own words. Each becomes a switch-like sensor your automations can trigger on — for example no_grid_import, grid_charge_battery. Leave empty if you do not need any.
data_description.coasting_permitted: Tells other systems that letting a room drift is acceptable during this rate.
data_description.demand_period: A marker only. The monthly demand charge is not calculated here.
data_description.daily_allowance_kwh: Zero for none. Some plans give a period free only up to a daily cap.
data_description.fallback_rate: Only used when there is an allowance: what the energy costs once it is spent.

day_patterns_menu.title: Day patterns
day_patterns_menu.description:
A day pattern is a group of days that share the same timetable — every day, or weekdays and weekends separately, or a summer and a winter version.

Most plans need only one.

```
{plan}
```

data_description.same_every_day: Leave this on unless weekends, weekdays or public holidays are priced differently.
data_description.days: Ignored while 'Every day is the same' is on. Public holidays only appear as a choice once you nominate a holiday sensor under the general settings.
data_description.season_from: Optional. Leave both empty for all year. A range may cross the new year, for example 11-01 to 03-31.
data_description.season_to: Optional. Leave both empty for all year.

day_pattern_duplicate.title: Duplicate a day pattern
day_pattern_duplicate.description: Copies the time periods, so a weekend or a season can be built from a shape that already works.

periods_menu.title: Time periods
periods_menu.description:
The hours of the day, each priced at one of your rates. Together they must cover the whole day exactly once.

```
{plan}
```

period_add.title: Time period
period_add.description:
The start time is included and the end time is not, so one period can end at 16:00 and the next begin at 16:00. A period that runs to midnight ends at 00:00.

```
{plan}
```

data_description.prices_include_gst: Australian bills quote prices with GST included. Most European and US rate sheets quote them without.
data_description.valid_from: Optional. Leave empty unless you are recording a plan that started on a known date.
data_description.valid_to: Optional. When your retailer reprices, set this and add a new channel for the new plan, so past costs stay correct against the price that was actually in force.
data_description.holiday_sensor: Optional. A Workday sensor from Home Assistant's built-in Workday integration, which is off on a public holiday. Needed only if holidays are priced differently.
data_description.import_energy_sensor: Optional. Needed only to count a daily energy allowance.

meter_create.title: Create a Utility Meter
meter_create.description:
One monthly total per rate will be created, named after these rates: {rates}

The helper belongs to Home Assistant's Utility Meter integration, not to this one. Renaming a rate later will not rename its total, and deleting this channel will not delete the helper.

data_description.source_energy_sensor: The kilowatt hour total you want split by rate — usually your grid import sensor.

meter_link.title: Keep the dropdown in step
meter_link.description:
Choose the tariff dropdowns to set to the rate in force whenever the rate changes. The tariff names on the helper must match your rate names exactly: {rates}

Leave empty to do nothing.

data.supply_charge_entities: Also create the supply charge pair

data_description.supply_charge_entities: The Energy dashboard has no field for a fixed daily charge. This creates a running cost sensor and a matching token energy sensor to add as a second grid consumption source.
